435.text: Inert gases are mixed in iodine vapours. Then there are ____ between them.
435.sol: There are several types of van der Waals attraction : dipole/dipole, dipole/induced-dipole and spontaneous-dipole/induced-dipole.The spontaneousdipole/induced-dipole attractions are also known as London dispersion forces. LDF are surprisingly strong but are only short range forces e.g. surface of neutral molecules or inert gases. All molecules have LDF and strength increases with the size/surface area of the molecule. In case of halogens, ( LDF ) increases as ( F ₂ < Cl ₂ < Br ₂ < I ₂ ).

1976.text: The respiratory centre in the brain is stimulated by
options: CO ₂ concentration in venous blood
O ₂ concentration in artery blood
CO ₂ concentration in artery blood
O ₂ concentration in venous blood.
1976.sol: Respiratory centre controls the rate of respiration. Respiratory centre is located in medulla oblongata and pons. It has the following components (i) inspiratory area - connected to inspiratory muscles, (ii) Pneum otaxic area, (iii) Expiratory area, (iv) chemosensitive area. Chemoreceptors located on carotid and aortic bodies are sensitive to carbon dioxide levels in arterial blood. They send information to respiratory centre. Oxygen does not have a significant direct effect on the respiratory centre of the brain.

83941.text: The toxin proteins, isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis , coded by which of the following genes would control cotton bollworms and corn borer, respectively ?
83941.sol: The toxin proteins encoded by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms. The toxin protein encoded by the gene cryIAb controls the corn borer. Therefore, the genes that control cotton bollworms and corn borer respectively are cryIAc and cryIAb . Answer: cryIAc and cryIAb

84045.subject: Zoology
84045.text: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by __________.
84045.sol: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by a valve formed of three muscular flaps or cusps, known as the tricuspid valve. The bicuspid or mitral valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle. The semilunar valves guard the openings of the right and left ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta, respectively. The sino-atrial node is a specialized cardiac musculature present in the right upper corner of the right atrium.

84177.sol: Haemoglobin is the protein that makes red blood corpuscles red and binds easily and reversibly with oxygen. Normal values for haemoglobin are 14-20 ~g / 100 ~mL of blood in infants, 13-18 ~g / 100 ~mL in adult male and 12-16 ~g / 100 ~mL in adult females. Haemoglobin is made up of protein globin bound to the red haem pigment. The globin consists of four polypeptide chains-2 alpha and 2 beta. 84362.sol: Diversification in plant life appeared due to long periods of evolutionary changes. Earlier, the plants were thalloid and there were no differentiation among root, stem and leaves. Vascular tissues were absent as in alglae and bryophytes. In pteridophytes, seed habit was observed for the first time. Gymnosperm consists of vascular tissue and naked seed habitat. Angiosperms showed secondary growth, along with fruit formation.

When HIV replicates rapidly in helper T-lymphocytes and damages large number of these
With 15 days of sexual contact with an infected person

84540.sol: HIV enters into T-lymphocytes, replicates and produces progeny viruses. The progeny viruses released in the blood other helper T-lymphocytes. 85416.text: Cu ions released from copper-releasing Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs)
85416.sol: Cu ions release by copper-releasing intrauterine devices suppresses sperm motility. Intrauterine devices are inserted by doctors in the uterus through the vagina. They are available as the non-medicated IUDs, copper-releasing IUDs, and hormone-releasing IUDs, these IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus and the Cu ions suppress sperm's motility and fertilizing capacity. So, the correct answer is 'Suppress sperm motility'.

This results in sp^3 hybridization (tetrahedral) and no unpaired electrons (

119271.subject: Chemistry
119271.text: What is the IUPAC name of the major product formed when crotonaldehyde (but-2-enal) is treated with sodium borohydride ( NaBH ₄ )?
119271.sol: Crotonaldehyde (but-2-enal) contains two reducible functional groups: an aldehyde and a carbon-carbon double bond. Sodium borohydride ( NaBH ₄ ) is a mild reducing agent that selectively reduces the aldehyde group to a primary alcohol. It generally does not reduce isolated or conjugated carbon-carbon double bonds under standard conditions. Therefore, the reduction of but-2-enal yields but-2-en-1-ol. Reduction of both groups to yield butan-1-ol would require catalytic hydrogenation (e.g., H ₂/ Ni ). Answer: But-2-en

Answer: (X) - Holoenzyme, (Y) - Cofactor, (Z) -

They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, segmented and coelomate animals. The body of arthropods is covered by chitinous exoskeleton. The body consists of head, thorax and abdomen. 122707.subject: Botany

122707.sol: The root is covered at the apex by a thimble-like structure called the root cap (Figure 5.3). It protects the tender apex of the root as it makes its way through the soil. A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity. The cells of this region are very small, thin-walled and with dense protoplasm. They divide repeatedly. The cells proximal to this region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement and are responsible for the growth of the root in length. This region is called the region o

122754.sol: . Gynoecium is the female reproductive part of the flower and is made up of one or more carpels. A carpel consists of three parts namely stigma, style and ovary. Ovary is the enlarged basal part, on which lies the elongated tube, the style. The style connects the ovary to the stigma. The stigma is usually at the tip of the style and is the receptive surface for pollen grains. Each ovary bears one or more ovules attached to a flattened, cushion-like placenta. When more than one carpel is present, they may be free (a

123249.subject: Botany
123249.text: The given structure is found in which of the following plants?
123249.sol: Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean- shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses. the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the stomatal pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata.

If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
123475.sol: Cork consists of dead and compactly arranged rectangular cells that possess suberised cell walls. The cork cells contain tannins. Hence, they appear brown or dark brown in colour. The cork cells of some plants are filled with air. Cork prevents the loss of water by evaporation. It also protects the interior against entry of harmful micro-organisms, mechanical injury and extremes of temperature. Cork is light, compressible, nonreactive and sufficiently resistant to fire. It is used as stopper for bottles, shock abso

123741.subject: Botany
123741.text: What happens during metaphase I in meiosis?
options: Homologous chromosomes pair to form bivalents
Bivalents arrange on the equatorial plate
Homologous chromosomes move to the opposite poles with both their chromatids
123741.sol: During metaphase I the bivalents arrange on the equatorial plate. This is followed by anaphase I in which homologous chromosomes move to the opposite poles with both their chromatids. Each pole receives half the chromosome number of the parent cell. In telophase I, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear. Meiosis II is similar to mitosis. During anaphase II the sister chromatids separate. Thus at the end of meiosis four haploid cells are formed.

123840.subject: Botany
123840.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): During the diplotene stage of meiosis I, the recombined homologous chromosomes of a bivalent do not separate completely from each other. Reason (R): The synaptonemal complex remains intact and stabilizes the bivalents throughout the diplotene stage. In the light of the above statements, choose the
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
123840.sol: During the diplotene stage, the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents have a tendency to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers, forming X-shaped structures called chiasmata. Thus, they do not separate completely, making the Assertion true. The beginning of the diplotene stage is recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex, not its maintenance. Therefore, the Reason is false. Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

126762.subject: Botany
126762.text: Identify the competitive inhibitor of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase and the specific substrate it structurally resembles, respectively.
126762.sol: The enzyme succinic dehydrogenase acts on its normal substrate, succinate. Malonate acts as a competitive inhibitor of this enzyme because its molecular structure closely resembles that of succinate. Due to this structural similarity, malonate competes with succinate for the substrate binding site of the enzyme. Thus, the competitive inhibitor is malonate and the substrate it resembles is succinate. Reversing the order or confusing malonate with malate leads to incorrect choices. 133090.subject: Zoology
133090.text: During which geological period of evolution did the greatest diversification of life occurred on the earth?

133751.subject: Zoology
133751.text: What is the effluent from the primary settling tank used for?
133751.sol: Primary treatment basically involves physical removal of particles – large and small – from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation. These are removed in stages; initially, floating debris is removed by sequential filtration. Then the grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by sedimentation. All solids that settle form the primary sludge, and the supernatant forms the effluent. The effluent from the primary settling tank is taken for secondary treatment.

95407.subject: Botany
95407.text: A phylum in which the digestion is intracellular as well as extracellular and polyp body form is seen includes organisms which:
options: Show internal fertilization and indirect development.
Have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening.
95407.sol: Polyp and medusa body forms with extracellular as well as intracellular digestion are seen in phylum Cnidaria. Cnidarians are diploblastic which have special stinging cells called cnidocytes. They show external fertilization with indirect development. They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening (Blind Sac body plan).

96041.subject: Botany
96041.text: Select the option having all correct statements. a ER divide the intercellular space into two distinct compartments. b The cis and the trans face of the Golgi body are entirely different but interconnected. c Lysosomes are the single membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi body. d In plant cells, the vacuole can occupy up to 90 percent of the volume of the cell.
96041.sol: ER divide the intercellular space into two distinct compartments, luminal chamber and extra luminal chamber. Cis and trans face of golgi body are entirely different but interconnected. Lysosomes are formed by golgi body. Vacuole in a plant cell can occupy upto 90 % volume.

96138.text: With respect to bacterial pilus, which of the following statements is not true?
options: They are made up of pilin protein.
They play an important role in movement.
96138.sol: Pilus or pili are surface structures of the bacteria but do not play a role in motility. The pili are elongated tubular structures made up of a special protein. In some bacteria, they are known to help attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.

96181.subject: Botany
96181.text: The spindle fibres are made up of _______ protein.
96181.sol: Spindle fibres are formed of microtubules, which play an important role in movement of chromosomes and centrioles during cell division. Biochemically a profilament of microtubule is made of a protein called tubulin. Tubulin is an acidic protein, which occurs in two different forms called α -tubulin and β -tubulin. Cytoplasmic microtubules are highly dynamic structures constantly forming and dis-appearing depending on cell activities. Myosin is fibrous functional protein of muscle. 96351.subject: Botany
96351.text: Pick up the CORRECT statement from the following: a . The spindle formation is anastral in plant cell while amphiastral in an animal cell. b . DNA replicates once in mitosis and twice in meiosis. c . Equational division, as well as reduction division, occurs in both, sexually and asexually reproducing organisms.
96351.sol: The DNA replication takes place only once during the S phase of mitosis. The equational division also known as mitosis takes place in organisms having both modes of reproduction, asexual as well as sexual, both meiosis or reductional division involves the fusion of gametes and reduction of the chromosome by half, found only in sexual reproduction. In plant cells, the spindle formation is anastral (without asters) and in animal cells spindle has two asters, one at each pole of the spindle.

96374.subject: Botany
96374.text: In which phase of the cell cycle, the amount of DNA in a cell remains constant at 4C level, considering that the initial amount of DNA was 2C?
96374.sol: G 1 phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. During G 1 phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time, the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C, then it increases to 4C. 96381.subject: Botany
96381.text: The statement, 'Tiger is in the apex of food chain', indicates
options: Tiger is dependent upon a large number of herbivores
96381.sol: Tiger is the top consumer in a food chain. It can feed upon lower carnivores as well as herbivores. Herbivores are dependent upon producers (i.e., green plants) for their food. Thus, indirectly it is also linked with trees (i.e., primary producers).

96435.subject: Botany
96435.text: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium, etc., present in the soil at any given time is referred to as the
96435.sol: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium, etc., present in the soil at any given time, is referred to as the standing state. It varies in different kinds of ecosystems and also on a seasonal basis

96450.subject: Botany
options: Energy always decreases with increases in trophic level.
Secondary succession is faster than primary succession.
Ecological pyramids cannot explain all the vital functions of any ecosystem.
The amount of nutrients present in the soil at any given time is referred to as the standing crop.
96450.sol: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium, present in the soil at any given time is referred to as the standing state. Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area.

96610.subject: Botany
96610.text: Biological equilibrium is maintained with the help of
96610.sol: Two process in ecosystem which are necessary to maintain biological equilibrium is photosynthesis and the other is respiration. Photosynthesis is source of energy for all organism on earth and maintains oxygen balance. Respiration is important in carbon cycle.

97517.sol: The main form of the haplontic life cycle is haploid and diploid zygote is formed in this cycle for a short period of time and this type of life cycle is found in Spirogyra . 97599.sol: Electron transport system (ETS) is present in the inner membrane of mitochondrial. Electrons from NADH produced in the mitochondrial matrix during TCA cycle are oxidised by an NADH dehydrogenase (complex I), and are transferred to ubiquinone located within the inner membrane. Ubiquinone also receives reducing equivalents via FADH2 (complex II) that is generated during oxidation of succinate in the TCA cycle. 303796.text: When the image is formed at the near point ( 25 cm ) of a normal eye, a simple microscope exhibits a magnifying power of 3.0 . Determine the focal length of the microscope.

305814.subject: Physics
305814.text: An ideal gas is taken from an initial state i to a final state f such that the ratio of its pressure to its absolute temperature is maintained constant. Determine the work done by the gas.
305814.sol: Given that the ratio of pressure to absolute temperature is constant: P T = constant From the ideal gas equation, we have: PV = nRT P T = nR V Since P T is constant, nR V must also be constant. For a given amount of ideal gas, n and R are constants, which implies that the volume V of the gas remains constant throughout the process. Since the volume is constant ( dV = 0 ), the process is isochoric. The work done by the gas is given by: W = P , dV = 0

6a7a1ff896970407d4a4c44c.text: A protection circuit consists of a Zener diode having a breakdown voltage of 5 V and a red light emitting diode (LED) with a turn-on voltage of 2 V connected in series with a current-limiting resistor of 300 . This entire combination is placed across a variable DC power supply. If the maximum power rating of the Zener diode is 50 mW , the maximum safe voltage of the DC power supply is _____ V .
6a7a1ff896970407d4a4c44c.sol: The maximum safe current through the Zener diode is determined by its maximum power rating: I_ max = P_ max V_ Z = 50 10⁻³ 5 = 10 mA Since the components are connected in series, this is the maximum allowable current for the entire circuit. The maximum safe voltage of the DC supply is the sum of the voltage drops across the Zener diode, the LED, and the resistor at this maximum current: V_ total = V_ Z + V_ LED + I_ max R V_ total = 5 + 2 + (10 10⁻³ 300) V_ total = 7 + 3 = 10 V . Answer: 10

6a7a1ff84905313ad325eede.sol: For a compound to dissolve in both aqueous NaOH and aqueous NaHCO ₃ , it must be a stronger acid than carbonic acid ( H ₂ CO ₃ ).
